note: Anchor verses are looked up live in the bundled KJV text.

reflections.title: He did not cling to His glory
reflections.trial: The eternal Son emptied Himself, took the form of a servant, and was born into a poor family under an occupying army. He grew up in a town of no reputation and worked with His hands for most of His life.
reflections.reflection: The God who made the world entered it as a child who had to be carried. Everything He laid aside, He laid aside willingly, and He did it for people who would not recognise Him.
reflections.practice: Take the lower place today in one situation where you could rightfully claim the higher one.

reflections.title: Moved with compassion
reflections.trial: He saw the crowds as sheep without a shepherd, scattered and exhausted. He was interrupted constantly by the sick, the grieving and the desperate, and He healed them even when He had gone away to rest.
reflections.reflection: His compassion was not a mood but a movement. He did not merely feel for people, He stopped, turned aside, and gave them what they needed at cost to Himself.
reflections.practice: Let one interruption today become the actual work instead of the thing keeping you from it.

reflections.title: He washed their feet
reflections.trial: On the night He was betrayed, knowing all things were given into His hands, He took a towel and washed the feet of twelve men, including the one about to sell Him for silver.
reflections.reflection: He served Judas. Greatness in His kingdom is measured by the basin and the towel, and it is offered to people who have not earned it and will not repay it.
reflections.practice: Do one unseen, unglamorous task for someone who cannot thank you for it.

reflections.title: Not my will, but thine
reflections.trial: In the garden His soul was exceeding sorrowful unto death. He prayed until His sweat was as great drops of blood, and asked three times that the cup pass from Him, while His closest friends slept.
reflections.reflection: He was not a stoic. He wanted the suffering removed and said so plainly, and then He submitted anyway. Obedience did not require Him to pretend the cost was small.
reflections.practice: Tell God honestly what you dread, and then hand Him the decision without taking it back.

reflections.title: Father, forgive them
reflections.trial: He was betrayed, denied, falsely tried, flogged, mocked and crucified. In the hours of His dying He was taunted by the people He came to save.
reflections.reflection: His first word from the cross was mercy for His executioners. He bore the punishment that belonged to others and prayed for them while they drove the nails.
reflections.practice: Name someone who wronged you and pray for their good by name, without conditions.

reflections.title: The firstfruits of them that slept
reflections.trial: He was truly dead and truly buried. His followers scattered in grief and fear, believing the story had ended in defeat.
reflections.reflection: The resurrection is not a symbol of renewal but an event in history that changes the standing of everyone who trusts Him. Because He lives, no faithfulness is finally wasted.
reflections.practice: Do the right thing today in a matter where you will never see the result.

reflections.title: Woe is me, for I am undone
reflections.trial: Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, and his first response was not delight but ruin: he was a man of unclean lips among a people of unclean lips, and he expected to die.
reflections.reflection: Seeing God truly makes a person honest about himself. Only after the coal touched his lips and his sin was purged could he say, Here am I, send me.
reflections.practice: Confess one specific sin by name rather than in general terms, and receive the cleansing before you try to serve.

reflections.title: Despised and rejected of men
reflections.trial: Isaiah prophesied for decades to a nation that would not listen, and was told at his commissioning that they would hear but not understand. Tradition holds he was martyred under Manasseh.
reflections.reflection: Seven centuries before the crucifixion he described a servant wounded for our transgressions, by whose stripes we are healed. He preached a hope he would not live to see.
reflections.practice: Keep faithful in a duty that is producing no visible fruit right now.

reflections.title: They shall renew their strength
reflections.trial: He wrote to a people facing exile, loss of their temple and the collapse of everything that had marked them as God’s people.
reflections.reflection: To wait on the Lord is not passivity but the active refusal to seek strength elsewhere. Even youths faint, but those who wait mount up with wings as eagles.
reflections.practice: Refuse one shortcut today that would work but would mean acting without God.

reflections.title: Why persecutest thou me?
reflections.trial: Saul held the coats at Stephen’s stoning and dragged believers from their homes to prison. He was struck blind on the Damascus road and spent three days without sight, food or water.
reflections.reflection: Christ said the persecution was against Him, not merely His people. The chief of sinners became the apostle to the Gentiles, which means no one is past mercy.
reflections.practice: Stop defending a position you have begun to suspect is wrong.

reflections.title: My strength is made perfect in weakness
reflections.trial: Paul was given a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet him. He begged the Lord three times to remove it, and it was not removed.
reflections.reflection: The answer to his prayer was sufficient grace rather than a cure. God declined to remove the weakness because the weakness was the place His power would rest.
reflections.practice: Stop hiding one limitation, and let someone see where you actually need help.

reflections.title: In perils oft
reflections.trial: Five times he received thirty-nine stripes, three times he was beaten with rods, once stoned and left for dead, three times shipwrecked, a night and a day in the deep, often in hunger, cold and nakedness.
reflections.reflection: He listed these not to be admired but to answer men who measured ministry by comfort and eloquence. He counted it all loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ.
reflections.practice: Measure a decision today by faithfulness rather than by what it costs you in comfort.

reflections.title: I have learned to be content
reflections.trial: He wrote about contentment from a Roman prison, uncertain whether the outcome would be release or execution, and dependent on gifts from a poor church.
reflections.reflection: He says he learned it, which means it was not his natural temper. Contentment is a trained skill, learned in both abasement and abundance.
reflections.practice: Name three things you already have that you have stopped thanking God for.

reflections.title: Go yet, love a woman
reflections.trial: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, who was unfaithful to him, and to bear the public shame of it. When she had gone from him he was told to go and buy her back and love her again.
reflections.reflection: His marriage was a living sermon about God’s covenant love for an unfaithful people. He paid to redeem the wife who had betrayed him, which is what God does for us.
reflections.practice: Choose to keep a commitment to someone who has not kept theirs to you.

reflections.title: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice
reflections.trial: Hosea preached to a prosperous, religiously busy nation whose worship had become a performance while it oppressed the poor and chased other gods.
reflections.reflection: God is not impressed by religious observance offered instead of a changed heart. He wants mercy and the knowledge of Himself more than He wants the offering.
reflections.practice: Check whether a religious habit of yours has become a substitute for obeying something you already know.

reflections.title: The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away
reflections.trial: In a single day Job lost his oxen, sheep, camels, servants and all ten of his children. Soon after he was struck with boils from the sole of his foot to his crown, and his wife told him to curse God and die.
reflections.reflection: He worshipped before he understood, and he never received an explanation. He mourned loudly and honestly, and he did not charge God foolishly.
reflections.practice: Worship once this week without first requiring an explanation for something that hurts.

reflections.title: Miserable comforters are ye all
reflections.trial: Three friends sat with him seven days in silence, which was their best gift. Then they spoke, insisting his suffering proved hidden sin, and pressed that charge for chapters.
reflections.reflection: They defended God with arguments God later rebuked. Their theology was tidy and their timing was cruel, and Job had to pray for them in the end.
reflections.practice: Sit with someone in trouble without offering an explanation for their suffering.

reflections.title: Now mine eye seeth thee
reflections.trial: After thirty-seven chapters of unanswered argument, God answered out of the whirlwind with questions rather than reasons, asking where Job was when the foundations of the earth were laid.
reflections.reflection: Job never learned why. He received something better than an explanation, which was God Himself, and that was enough to quiet him.
reflections.practice: Bring God a question you have been demanding He answer, and ask instead to know Him better in it.

reflections.title: Ye thought evil against me
reflections.trial: Sold into slavery by his brothers, falsely accused by Potiphar’s wife, imprisoned for years and forgotten by the man he helped.
reflections.reflection: He told his brothers plainly that what they did was evil, and that God meant it unto good. He named the wrong honestly and still forgave and fed them.
reflections.practice: Forgive without pretending the wrong done to you was small.

reflections.title: I am slow of speech
reflections.trial: A fugitive murderer keeping sheep for forty years, Moses argued with God at the bush through five objections before going, and afterwards led a people who repeatedly wanted to stone him.
reflections.reflection: God did not agree that Moses was adequate. He said, I will be with thy mouth, which was a better answer than a change of temperament.
reflections.practice: Say yes to one duty you feel unqualified for, and prepare for it anyway.

reflections.title: Create in me a clean heart
reflections.trial: David committed adultery with Bathsheba, arranged Uriah’s death to hide it, and lived nearly a year in unrepentant silence until Nathan confronted him.
reflections.reflection: When caught he did not manage the scandal, he confessed. He asked not merely for pardon but for a clean heart and a right spirit, wanting the sin itself gone.
reflections.practice: Ask someone you trust to tell you plainly about a fault you defend.

reflections.title: It is enough; now, O Lord, take away my life
reflections.trial: The day after the triumph on Carmel, Jezebel threatened him and he fled a day’s journey into the wilderness, sat under a juniper tree and asked to die.
reflections.reflection: God’s first treatment was not rebuke but food and sleep, twice, and then a still small voice. He also corrected Elijah’s belief that he was the only one left.
reflections.practice: Treat exhaustion as exhaustion: sleep, eat, and postpone the big conclusion about your life.

reflections.title: A burning fire shut up in my bones
reflections.trial: He preached forty years without a recorded convert, was beaten and put in the stocks, thrown into a miry dungeon, and saw the city he loved destroyed exactly as he had warned.
reflections.reflection: He complained bitterly to God, said he had been deceived, and resolved to stop speaking, and could not. Faithfulness and anguish lived in him at the same time.
reflections.practice: Bring your complaint to God directly instead of carrying it silently or airing it to everyone else.

reflections.title: His windows being open
reflections.trial: Taken captive as a youth, renamed and trained to serve a pagan court, he served under four kings and was thrown to lions in old age for praying.
reflections.reflection: When the decree was signed he changed nothing. He prayed as he did aforetime, openly, without protest or concealment, because the habit was already settled.
reflections.practice: Keep one ordinary spiritual habit today exactly as you would if no one objected.

reflections.title: Whither thou goest, I will go
reflections.trial: A Moabite widow with no children and no security, she left her homeland to follow a bitter mother-in-law who told her to go back, and gleaned in the fields to keep them both alive.
reflections.reflection: Her covenant loyalty was offered when it looked like a bad decision. She was brought into the line of David and of Christ Himself.
reflections.practice: Keep a promise this week that has become inconvenient.

reflections.title: If I perish, I perish
reflections.trial: An orphan taken into a foreign king’s harem, she learned of a decree to destroy her people and knew that approaching the king unbidden could cost her life.
reflections.reflection: Mordecai warned that silence would not save her, and asked whether she had come to the kingdom for such a time as this. She fasted three days and then went.
reflections.practice: Speak up once where staying quiet would be safer and someone else would pay for your silence.

reflections.title: I knew that thou art a gracious God
reflections.trial: Jonah fled from his commission, was thrown into the sea and swallowed by a great fish. When Nineveh repented he was angry enough to die, because he had not wanted them spared.
reflections.reflection: His problem was never doubt about God’s mercy but resentment of it. God’s last word to him is a question about whether He may pity a city of a hundred and twenty thousand.
reflections.practice: Ask whether you would be glad if someone you resent received grace.

reflections.title: Yet I will rejoice in the Lord
reflections.trial: He asked God why violence went unpunished, and the answer was worse than the question: God was raising up the Chaldeans, a crueller nation, as the instrument of judgment.
reflections.reflection: He ends by saying that though the fig tree does not blossom and there is no herd in the stall, yet he will rejoice. His joy is anchored in God, not in circumstances.
reflections.practice: Write down one thing about God that stays true regardless of how this month goes.

reflections.title: Lovest thou me?
reflections.trial: He swore he would die with Christ, then denied Him three times before a servant girl and a charcoal fire, and went out and wept bitterly.
reflections.reflection: The risen Christ restored him beside another charcoal fire, asking three times whether he loved Him and commissioning him three times. Failure was not the end of his usefulness.
reflections.practice: Return to a duty you abandoned after failing at it.

reflections.title: Lay not this sin to their charge
reflections.trial: Chosen to serve tables, he preached to the council, was dragged out and stoned while the witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
reflections.reflection: He died as his Master did, asking forgiveness for his killers. The man who watched him die became the apostle Paul.
reflections.practice: Ask God to bless someone who has cost you something, and mean it.

reflections.title: Be it unto me according to thy word
reflections.trial: A young woman in a small town accepted a pregnancy that would look to everyone like disgrace, risked her betrothal, and was later told a sword would pierce her own soul.
reflections.reflection: She asked one honest question, received an answer, and consented. Years later she stood at the cross and watched the sword arrive.
reflections.practice: Give God a yes today before you can see how it will turn out.

reflections.title: He must increase, but I must decrease
reflections.trial: He drew crowds into the wilderness, then watched them leave for Jesus. He was imprisoned by Herod, sent from prison to ask whether Jesus was truly the one, and was beheaded at a banquet.
reflections.reflection: He called himself the friend of the bridegroom, whose joy is fulfilled by hearing the bridegroom’s voice. He measured success by another man’s rising.
reflections.practice: Praise someone publicly for something you wanted credit for.

reflections.title: My Lord and my God
reflections.trial: He refused to believe the reports of the resurrection without seeing the print of the nails, and spent a week among rejoicing friends while remaining unconvinced.
reflections.reflection: Christ came back a week later specifically for him and offered His hands and His side. He met the doubt with evidence rather than with contempt.
reflections.practice: Bring an honest doubt to God rather than pretending you do not have it.
